en.headline: Mainland monk remanded over alleged theft of Monkey King statue from Tsuen Wan temple
en.dek: Zha Jianxin, 57, a two-way permit holder from Shenzhen, appeared in West Kowloon Court charged with stealing a HK$2,000 copper statue of Sun Wukong from Lung Mo Temple.
body: A 57-year-old mainland Chinese monk was remanded in custody on Wednesday after being charged with theft of a Monkey King statue from a temple in Tsuen Wan.

Zha Jianxin, who holds a two-way permit and lives in Shenzhen, is accused of taking a copper statue of Sun Wukong valued at HK$2,000 from near the entrance of Lung Mo Temple on 24 August. The statue belongs to the temple.

At West Kowloon Magistrates’ Courts, Zha did not apply for bail. He asked the magistrate for permission to telephone a fellow monk to say he would temporarily be unable to chant scriptures for him; the request was granted. The case was adjourned to 23 September for further inquiries including immigration records.

zh.headline: 內地和尚涉偷荃灣龍母佛堂孫悟空神像還押
zh.dek: 57歲雙程證持有人查建新被控於8月24日在荃灣龍母佛堂附近偷取價值2,000元銅製孫悟空神像，西九龍裁判法院還押至9月23日再訊。
body: 一名57歲內地和尚周三在西九龍裁判法院被控一項盜竊罪，暫毋須答辯，還押候訊。
被告查建新持雙程證，報稱居於深圳。控罪指他於8月24日在荃灣老圍上角山8號近龍母佛堂入口路邊，偷取一個屬該佛堂、價值港幣2,000元的銅製孫悟空神像。
被告沒有申請保釋，但要求致電友人告知暫時未能為對方念經，獲裁判官批准。案件押後至9月23日再訊，以待取得出入境紀錄等資料。
